title: A Study of Risvutatug Rezetecan in Combination With Atezolizumab in Participants With Extensive Stage Small Cell Lung Cancer (EMBOLD-SCLC-303)
official: A Phase 3 Randomized Open-Label Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Risvutatug Rezetecan in Combination With Atezolizumab in Participants With Newly Diagnosed Extensive Stage Small Cell Lung Cancer
summary: Extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) is an aggressive type of lung cancer. Current treatment options are limited, and response to treatment may not last long. Outcomes are especially poor when the cancer has spread to the brain. This study tests whether a new treatment: risvutatug rezetecan (Ris-Rez) with atezolizumab works better than standard of care treatment. Ris-Rez is designed to deliver cancer-killing medicine directly to cancer cells. Atezolizumab helps the immune system attack cancer cells. Researchers will see if this combination helps people live longer and keeps the cancer from getting worse.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Is at least 18 years of age or the legal age of consent in the jurisdiction in which the study is taking place at the time of signing the informed consent form (ICF).
* Has histologically or cytologically confirmed extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) at initial diagnosis and at trial entry and has received no prior systemic therapies for SCLC, with 1 exception where participants who have received one cycle of etoposide and carboplatin with or without atezolizumab are eligible
* Is capable of giving signed informed consent including compliance with the requirements and restrictions listed in the ICF and protocol.
* Has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 or 1.
* Has adequate organ function.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Has symptomatic central nervous system (CNS) metastases, CNS metastases with hemorrhagic features, or leptomeningeal disease.
* Has known allergy or hypersensitivity to study intervention components or excipients.
* Has any evidence of current interstitial lung disease or non-infectious pneumonitis or a prior history of interstitial lung disease (ILD) or non-infectious pneumonitis requiring high dose steroids or suspected ILD/non-infectious pneumonitis that cannot be ruled out by imaging.
* Has moderate to severe pulmonary disease or current clinically significant pulmonary compromise that, in the investigator's judgment, could jeopardize safety or study conduct.
* Has clinically significant bleeding symptoms, bleeding tumors, or significant bleeding tendency within 1 month prior to first dose.
* Known active infectious diseases requiring systemic treatment or known human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).
* Has received any prior systemic anticancer treatment for the disease under study.
* Has received any prior therapy with a Topoisomerase-1 (TOP1i), including antibody-drug conjugates that are effectively loaded as TOP1i, or treatment targeting B7-H3.
* Has severe, uncontrolled, or active cardiovascular disorders.
